pairs.subject: node-boot-and-declarative-bootstrap
pairs.evidence: app/_lib/sanity-checks.ts:1 The supposed 'startup sanity-check' module is actually the per-analysis trust ledger. The other files are a post-response task deferrer and a per-call origin resolver. None of the context's five files holds a boot step, reload handler, first-start bootstrap, config-born object or seal: grepping them for boot/seal/reload/restart/marker/seed/startup/listen found only comment mentions of 'boot' and the unrelated WARN_MARKERS regex, and grepping app/_lib for SIGHUP, verify-only, restart-only and bootstrap_marker found nothing.

techniques.evidence: app/_lib/public-base-url.ts:136 The origin-conflict 'boot warning' fires lazily on the first publicBaseUrl() call, not as a step in a startup graph. This module has no startup rung of its own, and the readiness aggregation lives in app/_lib/readiness.ts, which is outside this context.
app/_lib/public-base-url.ts:143 The configuration is process env, read on each call. There is no reload signal or reload path here that would need a reloadable/restart-only partition.
app/_lib/after-response.ts:32 The only scheduled work is an in-code callback deferred past the response. There is no declarative bootstrap file or request chain.
